issues.t: Passenger airbag inflator can rupture (Takata recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning signs. In a crash the passenger airbag inflator can burst and throw metal pieces into the cabin.
issues.why: The Vibe uses a Takata passenger airbag inflator whose propellant breaks down over years of heat and humidity. Every model year is covered by recalls (including 15V-285, 15V-286, 16V-127, 16V-128, 16V-340, 17V-006, 18V-024, 18V-025 and 18V-883).
issues.next: Check your VIN on the NHTSA recall site today. If the recall is open, don't let anyone ride in the front passenger seat until a dealer replaces the inflator for free.

issues.t: Replacement passenger airbag may not open fully in heat (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. Cars that already had the airbag recall done may have received a replacement that doesn't unfold correctly in high heat.
issues.why: Some replacement passenger airbags installed under the earlier Takata recalls were folded in a way that can keep them from inflating properly when hot (recalls 19V-627 and 20V-039).
issues.next: Even if your airbag was already replaced, check your VIN again for this follow-up recall.

issues.t: Engine computer can crack and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Check engine light, harsh shifting, hard starting, or the engine shutting off while driving.
issues.why: Solder joints or parts inside the engine control module can crack (recall 10V-387).
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have a dealer check your VIN. The recall inspects and replaces the engine computer for free.

issues.t: Accelerator pedal can stick (recall)
issues.sym: The gas pedal feels stiff, comes back up slowly, or stays partly down.
issues.why: Condensation can add friction inside the pedal's sensor (recall 10V-018).
issues.next: If it happens, brake firmly and shift to Neutral. Make sure the pedal recall was done.

issues.t: Floor mat can trap the gas pedal (recall)
issues.sym: The gas pedal sticks down, causing the car to speed up.
issues.why: A loose or wrong floor mat can catch the pedal (recall 10V-024).
issues.next: Use only the correct mat, held by its clips, and never stack mats. Check the recall.

issues.t: Power window master switch can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: The driver's window switch feels hot, works erratically, smells burnt or melts.
issues.why: The switch may lack enough grease, letting it short and overheat (recalls 12V-491 and 15V-689).
issues.next: Stop using the switch if it smells or feels hot, and get the recall done.

issues.t: Driver airbag light from a damaged spiral cable (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on, and the horn may stop working.
issues.why: A flat cable in the steering column can get damaged so the driver airbag is disconnected (recall 14V-168).
issues.next: Have the airbag light checked and the recall done right away.

issues.t: Brake assist can freeze in extreme cold (recall)
issues.sym: In very cold weather the brake pedal feels hard and the car takes longer to stop.
issues.why: Moisture can freeze in the brake booster vacuum port (recall 09V-392).
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check that the recall was done, especially if you live somewhere very cold.

issues.t: Airbags can go off without a crash (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag light may be on. In rare cases the front airbags or belt tighteners fire without a crash.
issues.why: Electrical noise or an internal short can damage the airbag control module (recalls 13V-029 and 15V-043).
issues.next: Check the recall with your VIN.

issues.t: Door glass can come loose from the window regulator (recall)
issues.sym: A front window drops, tilts or won't go up.
issues.why: The bolts holding the glass to the regulator can loosen (recall 08V-162).
issues.next: Check the recall; the dealer reattaches the glass with new bolts.

issues.t: Rear brake and hub bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or wobble from the rear wheels.
issues.why: Bolts for the rear brake and hub assembly may not have been tightened enough at the factory (recall 02V-074).
issues.next: Check the recall with your VIN.

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption
issues.sym: Burning about a quart every 1,000 miles or more, low oil with no leak, and sometimes the dipstick reads empty.
issues.why: The 2.4L engine's piston rings can wear early. Toyota covered the same engine on its own cars, but owners say GM did not extend coverage for the Vibe.
issues.next: Check the oil at every fill-up and top it up. Running it low can ruin the engine. A shop can do an oil consumption test to confirm.

issues.t: Manual transmission bearing noise or failure
issues.sym: A whine or clicking from the transmission that gets louder with speed and goes away when you press the clutch. It can end in full transmission failure.
issues.why: Bearings inside the 5-speed manual transmission wear out, most often around 85,000 miles.
issues.next: Get it checked when the noise starts. Rebuilding early with new bearings can prevent a failed transmission.

issues.t: Wheel bearing hum
issues.sym: A hum or growl that gets louder at highway speed.
issues.why: Wheel bearings and hubs are the most-reported repair on the Vibe, especially at higher mileage.
issues.next: Have the bearing checked and replaced before it gets loose.

issues.t: Alternator failure, battery light on
issues.sym: The battery warning light comes on, lights dim, or the car dies after the battery drains.
issues.why: The alternator is one of the most-reported Vibe repairs.
issues.next: If the battery light comes on while you're driving, turn off everything you don't need (A/C, radio, seat heaters) and drive only as far as a safe place off the road, not a long trip. If the temperature gauge climbs or the steering gets heavy, stop and turn the engine off. Your owner's manual may say what your car needs; follow it. Have the charging system tested. Rebuilt alternators are an option.

issues.t: Starter clicks but won't crank
issues.sym: A single click or nothing when you turn the key.
issues.why: A weak battery or worn starter are the usual causes.
issues.next: Test the battery first. If it is good, the starter likely needs replacing.

issues.t: Water pump leak
issues.sym: Low coolant, pink crusty residue or coolant spray near the drive belt, or a squeal before it fails.
issues.why: The water pump seal and bearing wear out.
issues.next: Top up with the right coolant and replace the pump before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Intake manifold gasket vacuum leak
issues.sym: Check engine light, rough idle or a hissing sound.
issues.why: The intake manifold gasket can leak air.
issues.next: The gasket is a simple part. Have a shop smoke-test the intake to confirm.

issues.t: Lean code (P0171) from a dirty airflow sensor
issues.sym: Check engine light with a 'system too lean' code, rough idle, weak power or stalling.
issues.why: A dirty mass airflow sensor is the most common cause, though vacuum leaks can do the same.
issues.next: Try cleaning the airflow sensor with MAF cleaner. Replace it if the code comes back.

issues.t: Check engine light from the rear oxygen sensor
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0138.
issues.why: The downstream oxygen sensor fails.
issues.next: Replacing the sensor is a simple job.

issues.t: Misfire from a failed ignition coil
issues.sym: Shaking, rough running, a flashing check engine light, misfire codes.
issues.why: Individual ignition coils fail.
issues.next: Replace the bad coil, and change all spark plugs if they are old.

issues.t: Oil leak from the valve cover or timing chain tensioner
issues.sym: Oil seeping at the top or back of the engine, or a burning-oil smell.
issues.why: The valve cover gasket and the timing chain tensioner seal harden and leak.
issues.next: Both fixes are fairly simple; don't let oil drip on the exhaust.

issues.t: Noisy drive belt tensioner
issues.sym: A rattle, chirp or squeal from the belt area at the front of the engine.
issues.why: The drive belt tensioner pulley wears out on the 1.8L.
issues.next: Replace the tensioner and belt together.

issues.t: Brake pedal pulsates from worn front rotors
issues.sym: The brake pedal or steering wheel shakes when braking.
issues.why: The front rotors wear unevenly.
issues.next: Replace or resurface the rotors with new pads.

issues.t: Sticking brake caliper
issues.sym: The car pulls, a burning smell, or one wheel very hot after driving.
issues.why: Brake calipers are among the most-reported Vibe repairs.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected; a stuck caliper wears pads and rotors fast.

issues.t: Clicking from the dash or blower problems
issues.sym: Clicking behind the dash when changing air settings, or a blower that works on only some speeds.
issues.why: The fresh/recirculate air door motor, blower motor and blower resistor are common repairs.
issues.next: A shop can find which part failed. These are fairly simple repairs.

issues.t: Exhaust leak or rattling heat shield
issues.sym: A louder exhaust, ticking, or a tinny rattle from under the car.
issues.why: Flex pipes rust through and heat shields come loose.
issues.next: A muffler shop can often weld or clamp it.

issues.t: Check engine light from the gas cap
issues.sym: Check engine light with an evaporative leak code.
issues.why: A worn or loose gas cap lets fuel vapor escape.
issues.next: Tighten the cap until it clicks. If the light stays on after a few drives, replace the cap.

issues.t: Rusted brake or fuel lines
issues.sym: Brake fluid leak, soft pedal, or a gas smell, mainly in salt-belt states.
issues.why: Steel brake and fuel lines under the car can corrode badly with age.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Have the lines inspected at every brake job. Replace rusty lines before they burst.
